messages.body_plain:

I am new to brainGraph and I am having some problem with the function "plot_brainGraph_gui" since the error message tells me: "could not find function 'plot_brainGraph_gui'".

Specifically, I was able to create a graph using the 'grafo' function (just for example: grafo=plot(graph1, plane ="sagittal", hemi = "L") but then it seems like there is no way to show it over an image from the template.
I am using R studio Version 1.1.453 for Windows. However, I tried to run the same script using R studio on Linux but the error message was the same.

Thanks in advance for your help.
Kind regards,

Francesca Magnani

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Error in plot_brainGraph_gui
messages.body_plain:
In the code you provided, "grafo" is the name of the return object; it is not the name of a function.
The "plot" function actually does not return any object, so you should not be assigning a variable to the function call. That is, the "grafo=" portion is unnecessary.

Could you please give me some pieces of information:

packageVersion('brainGraph')
packageVersion('igraph')
class(graph1)

You should make sure you have loaded the "brainGraph" package, and that your graph object "graph1" has for its class "brainGraph".
Thanks,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Error in plot_brainGraph_gui
messages.body_plain:
No need to apologize, it is not a waste of time.

You must load individual packages if they are not a part of "base" R; there are only a handful of base R packages, so this is going to be a common occurrence.

In your code above, you should replace "library(igraph)" with "library(brainGraph)", because "brainGraph" loads "igraph" already.
If you are using a custom brain atlas (as it appears you are, or at least a subset), then some extra work is needed. Please follow the structure of the other atlases; for more information you can see Chapter 1.4 of the User Guide: https://cwatson.github.io/files/brainGraph_UserGuide.pdf

You will need to provide a "data.table" which has the following information:
* name - the name of the region (which, in your example, are stored in the "ROI" variable)
* x.mni - the x-coordinate for the region (usually the center-of-mass or center-of-gravity, or some other summary)
* y.mni - same as "x.mni"
* z.mni - same as "x.mni"
* lobe - a *factor* variable which consists of the names of the lobes each region is a part of. In case this is not important to you, you can probably supply "dummy" values; e.g. "factor(rep(1, length(ROI)))"
* hemi - a *factor* variable which consists of the hemisphere for each region
* index - just an integer vector; it should start at 1 and end at the number of regions, e.g. "1:24"

I do not know what x/y/z coordinates you are using, but the other variables you can set easily; the following is an example that you will need to adjust:

library(data.table)
atlas24 <- data.table(name=ROI, lobe=factor(rep(1, length(ROI))), hemi=c('L', 'L', 'L', 'R', 'R', 'R', 'R', 'L', 'R', 'XX', 'R', 'L', 'L', 'R', 'L', 'R', 'XX', 'R', 'L'), index=1:length(ROI))

Note that for "hemi" I have typed "XX" for a couple values; this is because the ROI names did not indicate to me which hemisphere they are a part of, so you will have to enter the correct value. After the above command, you can do the following:

atlas24[, hemi := as.factor(hemi)]

Let me know if you need more help.
Chris

If you are using an atlas in which all regions are not the same size, and you are interested in the inter-regional covariance (of LGI), then yes the same is true.

messages.body_plain:
For "set_brainGraph_attr", there probably isn't an easy way aside from either running "debug" mode, or editing the function yourself, saving it to disk, and loading it when you want. Really the best thing in this case is to calculate your metrics of interest in your own function/script. I am currently working on updating "set_brainGraph_attr" to allow for any community detection algorithm (not just Louvain, as it currently is). For other metrics/algorithms, there aren't alternatives in the same way.

Only the red edges appear because all of the "blue" edges are negative, and there isn't a way to render this as a width. A workaround would be take the absolute value, assign it as a new edge attribute (say, "weight2"), and use that. However the edge weights are << 1 so will appear very faint; you may want to try using the exponential function "exp" instead.

The density of this graph is extremely high so you will not be able to see much detail, even if you remove vertex labels and reduce vertex size.

messages.body_plain:
Hello, yesterday I updated the package to v2.4.0. There are a couple new features (which you can always see in NEWS.md on Github):

* "hubness" is a new function that is used to calculate a vertex's "hubness"; see van den Heuvel (2010) for details. This function is now used to calculate the "num.hubs" attribute by "set_brainGraph_attrs" instead of basing it on betweenness centrality.

* "set_brainGraph_attrs" has a new argument called "clust.method". This lets you choose a clustering (community detection) algorithm different from Louvain, which was the previous default. See the documentation for that function, and also the User Guide in Chapter 5.3.

* A very minor change, but one that *could* affect users, is that the "density" graph attribute assigned by "set_brainGraph_attrs" is no longer rounded.

As always, let me know if you have any issues.
Chris
